items.title: [.NET] Add support for web export using static LibGodot

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

items.body:
This PR serves as an alternative to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/106125.

# Overview

Uses static LibGodot to link Godot as a library for web export.

A huge portion of this PR was adding LibGodot support to web platform and figuring out a way to pass a static library to the final step. In comparison the changes to the way mono itself works are minor.

LibGodot setup itself doesn't use the module mono and instead uses a simple interface written natively in C#. To initialize the module mono it now exports a function when LibGodot is enabled that can be called to set the initialization function for the module, this indirection allows us to call it early from the C# side and be sure that the module mono will safely check it later, and if it is set it will call it when the module begin initializing. Doing it this way preserves the normal order `GDMono::initialize` is initialized. The initialization function itself passes normal initialization from `InitializeFromGameProject`.

## Works:
- JS import and export with `[JSExport]`/`[JSImport]`.
- Single-threaded and multi-threaded builds.
- .NET 9 and .NET 10, currently only tested on demo.
- Normal build and Web AOT compilation enabled with `RunAOTCompilation`.
- It's basically a normal `browser-wasm` publish with a statically linked Godot to it, so everything that works on `browser-wasm` should work here, this was briefly tested with `System.Security.Cryptography` and `System.Net.Http.HttpClient`.

## Downsides:

### Major downsides:
- It will force the support for Emscripten 3.1.56 until C# Emscripten is updated (https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/113786).
- Can't export with GDExtensions supported, C# WASM can't be build with `-sMAIN_MODULE` flag.
- Currently it is not a problem, but CoreCLR also uses `Object` without namespace, so it causes duplicate symbols for `Object` vtable. If C# WASM will move to CoreCLR https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/121511 after updating Emscripten to be new enough to use `--allow-multiple-definition` https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/pull/97699 this won't be a problem.

### Small downsides:
- Slow to export, as it needs to link the whole Godot as a static library.
- Can't use Godot as an `lto` library.
- Always needs to use `wasm-tools` workload.
- C# emscripten cache is frozen, so some combination of flags can require the usage of `WasmCachePath`, on Windows this path needs to be on the same drive as the drive C# is installed on.
- C# multi-threading runs main C# thread as a worker thread https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/101421, https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/126438.
- C# multi-threading is incompatible with `webxr` for the same reason `proxy_to_pthread` is also incompatible.
- C# multi-threading JS interop doesn't allow sync `C#->JS->C#` or `JS->C#->JS`, with `jsThreadBlockingMode: 'ThrowWhenBlockingWait'` it allows sync `C#->JS` and `JS->C#`, but that's all. More info https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/101421#issuecomment-2072439395 and this seems also correct https://dev.to/lostbeard/blazor-wasms-deputy-thread-model-will-break-javascript-interop-heres-why-that-matters-1n9n.

## Hacks:
- Calls web's `_export_begin` after extracting templates. It's needed for passing the path to the extracted static library in `ExportPlugin.cs._ExportBegin`. I think it is possible to add a separate step after extracting templates, but before `_export_file` begins, but I'm not sure.
- Some functions needed stubs because they were missing.

Closes: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/70796.
Demo repo: https://github.com/NoctemCat/DotnetWebExportDemo.

Thanks to @GabCoolDude for help writing it, testing export on Windows, and testing it overall.

items.title: Apple: Add tvOS platform support

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

items.body: # Summary **Depends on** - #109975 tvOS platform support for Godot. ## What's included? - ✅ Debug and release templates for tvOS - ✅ Platform support in the Godot editor - ✅ Platform exporter for tvOS - ✅ Controller via SDL support - 🚫 Simulator support[^1] - 🚫 OpenGL ES[^2]; selects to Metal + mobile renderer automatically if OpenGL is configured [^1]: Metal simulator device features do not meet the minimum requirements for the mobile or forward+ renderers [^2]: tvOS only supports OpenGL ES 2.0; Godot requires ES 3.0 ## Outstanding Issues ### Menu / back button support tvOS has a similar behaviour to Android with a back (Siri Remote) / menu button (game controllers) that navigate back towards the home screen. We can leverage the existing APIs for Android: | API | Comment | | :---- | :---- | | `quit_on_go_back` | controls whether menu / back is delivered as an event to the application | | `WINDOW_EVENT_GO_BACK_REQUEST` | Sent when `quit_on_go_back` is `false` | | `NOTIFICATION_WM_GO_BACK_REQUEST` | Sent when `quit_on_go_back` is `false` | A suggested flow would be that a game would set `quit_on_go_back` to `false` whilst in play, so that when a user presses back / menu, the game intercepts and displays a pause menu to the user. Whilst the pause menu is active, the game should set `quit_on_go_back` to `true`, so that if the user presses back / home again, the game naturally exits to the home screen, providing the correct HIG experience for users. ### ⚠️ Quit / Exit behaviour Exiting an app is prohibited on Apple embedded platforms, namely iOS, visionOS and tvOS. The OS manages the lifetime and applications are suspended by user action, such as pressing the Menu / back button. These platforms ignore the return value of `Main::iteration` in their C++ implementations, where returning `true` normally signals the process should exit. If an Godot application quits, **it puts the entire game into an inconsistent state**, as `SceneTree::_quit` is now `true`, and certain processes no longer run correctly. There is no way for an end user or a Godot developer to fix this without force-quitting, and would be perceived as bugs by users. My recommendation is that that the following APIs and behaviours be changed for APPLE_EMBEDDED platforms only: | API | Comments | | :---- | :---- | | `SceneTree::quit(exit_code)` | Log a warning and do nothing | | Node::_process | If it returns true, log warning and do nothing | | Node::_physics_process| If it returns true, log warning do nothing | | SceneTree::quit_on_go_back | always `false` for tvOS | - *Bugsquad edit:* This PR closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/13532

items.title: Add cross-runtime C# web export module via shared-memory Worker

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

items.body:
## Summary

This PR adds an optional **`cross_runtime`** module for Godot 4.x web exports. It enables C# gameplay logic to run in a Web Worker while Godot C++ handles rendering on the main thread, using a shared-memory contract based on fixed offsets.

The module is self-contained, can be enabled or disabled at build time through SCons, and does not require changes to existing engine code.

---

## Problem

Official C# web export support is currently unavailable in Godot 4.x due to limitations around embedding the .NET runtime in the engine’s WASM build (see #70796).

I implemented a different technique to enable C# web exports.

---

## Solution

This module runs two runtimes side by side:

- **Godot (C++)** runs on the main thread and handles rendering.
- **.NET (C#)** runs in a dedicated Web Worker and handles simulation / game logic.

The two sides communicate through a single `SharedArrayBuffer` using a schema-defined memory layout with fixed offsets.

---

## How it works

1. Define a JSON schema describing the shared memory layout:
   - struct fields
   - entity counts
   - offsets
   - buffer sizes

2. Run the generator. It produces:
   - `memory_layout.h` - C++ contract 
   - `Bridge.cs` — matching C# contract with read/write helpers
   - a memory-contract correctness test

3. Implement the game logic:
   - C++ reads the shared buffer and renders entities
   - C# updates simulation state and writes results back

4. Build and export:
   - `scons platform=web`
   - `python build.py` to publish the C# worker

5. Run in the browser:
   - the main thread renders directly from shared memory
   - the worker performs simulation without per-entity bridge calls

---

## Architecture

```text
┌──────────────────────┐     Shared Memory     ┌─────────────────────┐
│  Godot Main Thread   │ ◄──── reads/writes ─► │  Web Worker (.NET)  │
│  - DotRenderer node  │                       │  - C# GameLogic     │
│  - MultiMesh draw    │                       │  - BulkRead/BulkWrite│
└──────────────────────┘                       └─────────────────────┘
```

I’m happy to receive feedback, discuss the approach, and make any changes the team feels are necessary.

items.title: [.NET] Add web export support

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

items.body:
Use Mono embedding APIs statically linked to load the Mono WASM runtime.

- The Mono runtime is fetched using the `GetRuntimePack` C# project. It needs the `wasm-tools` workload.
- The `GetRuntimePack` defines stub functions for all the function pointers we need to retrieve from C#, so the `PInvokeTableGenerator` includes them in the generated `pinvoke-table.h` file.
- Globalization doesn't work, so for now we're always enabling [invariant mode](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/runtime-config/globalization#invariant-mode).
- The Mono runtime uses stubs for their exported JavaScript functions, these need to be replaced with the real implementation in their `dotnet.runtime.js` module but we don't have an easy way to do that yet, which means some BCL APIs will not work (i.e.: crypto APIs)
- Closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/70796

> [!WARNING]
> This is still a work in progress, but it should be possible to export a C# game to web with some manual changes to the exported `.js` afterwards.

---

This PR was tested with the demo project: [Web .NET prototype](https://github.com/raulsntos/godot4-web-dotnet-prototype)

> [!NOTE]
> The demo project requires multi-threading, so make sure to change the `<WasmEnableThreads>` property to `true` to use the right Mono runtime.

items.title: Add SPM support for Apple Embedded plugins (.gdip)
items.body:
Add `spm_packages` key to the `[dependencies]` section of `.gdip` files, allowing plugins to declare Swift Package Manager dependencies with exact version pinning. The export pipeline generates the corresponding PBX entries in the Xcode project. --- Satisfies https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/4758. Thanks to @MileyHollenberg for initial integration with Cocoapods and telling us about SPM! Docs PR: https://github.com/godotengine/godot-docs/pull/11805 This PR prevents external plugins from having to rely on hacky workarounds (like post-export scripts) to add Swift Package Manager (SPM) dependencies. SPM is an excellent addition that will massively simplify the distribution and usage of iOS plugins because: - **No more post-export hacks**: Plugins no longer need complex export scripts to manipulate the generated Xcode project. - **One-Click Deploy**: SPM dependencies are natively resolved, guaranteeing that One-Click Deploy works out of the box. - **CI/CD Ready**: Natively supports automated build pipelines. - **Lighter, Cleaner Plugins**: Plugins become significantly smaller and simpler since heavy frameworks no longer need to be downloaded or embedded in the repository. --- This implementation was designed with developer experience in mind. The new `.gdip` format places the SPM packages directly inside the existing `[dependencies]` section: ```ini [dependencies] linked=[] embedded=[] system=["AppTrackingTransparency.framework"] capabilities=[] files=[] linker_flags=["-ObjC"] spm_packages=[ { "url": "https://github.com/googleads/swift-package-manager-google-mobile-ads.git", "version": "12.14.0", "products": ["GoogleMobileAds"] } ] ``` This approach is highly beneficial because: 1. **Self-Documenting**: The JSON-like `Array[Dictionary]` format exposes `url`, `version`, and `products` explicitly. 1. **Extensible**: More keys (like `platforms` or `checksums`) can be easily added in the future without breaking the parser. 1. **Familiarity**: It respects and closely follows how SPM natively structures its package dependencies. 1. **Deterministic Builds**: The export pipeline forces the Xcode requirement kind to be `exactVersion`. This guarantees reproducible builds and prevents bugs caused by dependencies silently updating to different versions. 1. **100% Backwards Compatible**: Older Godot versions parsing this `.gdip` file will simply ignore the `spm_packages` key safely. Data Flow Diagram: ```mermaid flowchart TD A["📄 .gdip file
[dependencies]
spm_packages=[...]"] -->|ConfigFile::load| B["load_plugin_config()
plugin_config_apple_embedded.cpp"] B -->|"Vector<SPMPackage>"| C["_export_apple_embedded_plugins()
editor_export_platform_apple_embedded.cpp"] C -->|Deduplicate by URL| D["PBX Generation"] D --> E["spm_packages
packageReferences list"] D --> F["spm_package_refs
XCRemoteSwiftPackageReference"] D --> G["spm_package_products
XCSwiftPackageProductDependency"] D --> H["modules_buildfile
PBXBuildFile"] D --> I["modules_buildphase
Frameworks build phase"] E --> J["_fix_config_file()
Template Substitution"] F --> J G --> J H --> J I --> J J -->|"$spm_packages
$spm_package_refs
$spm_package_products"| K["📦 project.pbxproj
Xcode resolves SPM at build time"] ``` --- Binaries: [poing-godot-admob-ios.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25670208/poing-godot-admob-ios.zip) Follow plugin tutorial if needed (just don't follow the Cocoapods step, this should be automatically now with SPM): https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TB7WhP8mieo Or: - Clone repository: https://github.com/poingstudios/godot-admob-plugin - Checkout to branch [205-prepare-for-spm-godot-47](https://github.com/poingstudios/godot-admob-plugin/tree/205-prepare-for-spm-godot-47) - Download the [poing-godot-admob-ios.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25670208/poing-godot-admob-ios.zip) - Paste into `res://ios/plugins` - Export the project

items.title: C#: Proof of concept — Multi-assembly script support for referenced projects

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

items.body:
# C#: Proof of concept — Multi-assembly script support for referenced projects > **This is a proof of concept (PoC) and request for feedback**, not a final implementation. I would greatly appreciate input from maintainers on the overall approach, architecture decisions, and whether this direction aligns with the project's roadmap — especially given the ongoing GDExtension discussion ([godot-proposals#7895](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/7895)). I'm happy to rework, split, or adapt any part of this based on feedback. ## Summary This PoC adds support for discovering and using C# scripts defined in external assemblies referenced via `` or ``. Currently, Godot only scans the main project assembly for scripts, so `[Export]` properties, `[GlobalClass]`, and lifecycle methods (`_Ready`, `_Process`, etc.) do not work for types in referenced assemblies. Multi-project C# solutions are standard practice in .NET for code organization, shared libraries, and modular architecture. This limitation has been reported across 25+ issues spanning 3 years since the .NET 6 migration. **Example project:** [GodotMultiAssemblyReference](https://github.com/matelq/GodotMultiAssemblyReference) — a complete working example with 3 assembly types (in-tree ProjectReference, in-tree Godot SDK ProjectReference, out-of-tree NuGet PackageReference). Clone it and open with the patched engine to test.
Screenshots (click to expand) ### Project structure (Rider solution explorer vs Godot FileSystem) ### Add Node dialog with external assembly scripts `EnemyController` is from an in-tree ProjectReference, `InventorySystem` is from an out-of-tree NuGet package. ### Select Script dialog Scripts from external assemblies (`csharp://` paths) are not shown — only `res://` scripts appear in this dialog. ### [Export] properties in Inspector In-tree ProjectReference (`EnemyController`): NuGet PackageReference (`InventorySystem`): ### Scene tree with nodes from multiple assemblies ### Warning when opening a script without source on disk Shown when attempting to open a NuGet package script in an external editor.
## What this PoC enables | Feature | In-tree ProjectReference | NuGet PackageReference | |---------|-------------------------|----------------------| | `[Export]` in Inspector | Yes | Yes | | `[GlobalClass]` in Add Node | Yes | Yes | | Lifecycle methods | Yes | Yes | | FileSystem panel | Yes | N/A (no source in `res://`) | | Open in external editor | Yes | Warning: "source not available" | ## Technical approach I'd like maintainer feedback on these design decisions in particular: ### 1. Assembly discovery via output directory scanning `LookupScriptsInReferencedAssemblies()` scans all DLLs in the main assembly's output directory for `[AssemblyHasScriptsAttribute]`, rather than using `Assembly.GetReferencedAssemblies()` (which the .NET compiler strips when no types are directly used in code). Called from both the editor path (`Main.cs`) and the export path (generated initializer). **Open question:** Is directory scanning acceptable, or would a manifest-based approach (e.g. MSBuild-generated list of script assemblies) be preferred? ### 2. `csharp://` path scheme for out-of-tree scripts Scripts outside `res://` (NuGet packages, truly external projects) get a synthetic `csharp://AssemblyName/Namespace.ClassName.cs` path. `ResourceFormatLoaderCSharpScript::load()` handles these by skipping source file loading and registering directly with `ScriptServer`. **Open question:** Is introducing a new URI scheme the right approach? Alternatives considered: `res://.godot/external/` stub files (rejected — creates physical files on disk), extending `res://` to support `../` paths (rejected — security implications). ### 3. Recommended project layout The PoC works best when `project.godot` is placed at the solution root: ``` MyGame/ <- project.godot here (res:// root) project.godot <- dotnet/project/project_directory = "MainProject" MainProject/ MyGame.csproj Player.cs <- res://MainProject/Player.cs Modules/ Combat/ Combat.csproj HealthComponent.cs <- res://Modules/Combat/HealthComponent.cs MyGame.slnx ``` This keeps all module source files under `res://` with full editor integration. A new `dotnet/project/project_directory` setting supports `.csproj` in a subdirectory. **Open question:** Is this layout acceptable as the recommended pattern, or should the engine be more flexible about project structures? ### 4. Other changes - `_register_csharp_global_class()` helper consolidates 3 duplicated registration blocks in `csharp_script.cpp` - `property_utils.cpp` stores/retrieves `csharp://` paths as `_custom_type_script` meta (no UID) - `ResourceFormatSaverCSharpScript::recognize()` rejects `csharp://` scripts - MSBuild `Sdk.targets` propagates `GodotProjectDir` to `ProjectReference` items - `InspectorPlugin` and `GodotSharpEditor` handle `csharp://` gracefully - Generic type virtual paths (`csharp://path:GenericType`) disambiguated with `FileAccess::exists()` fallback ## Testing - **42/42** source generator tests pass (2 new: `ExternalAssemblyInTree`, `ExternalAssemblyOutOfTree`) - Manual testing with [GodotMultiAssemblyReference](https://github.com/matelq/GodotMultiAssemblyReference) example project covering 3 scenarios: in-tree ProjectReference (Godot.NET.Sdk), in-tree ProjectReference (Microsoft.NET.Sdk + NuGet refs), out-of-tree NuGet PackageReference - Tested on Windows 11, .NET 8, Godot 4.7-dev ## Known limitations - NuGet package scripts cannot be opened in an external editor (no source on disk) — shows a warning - `SourceFile` embeds the build machine's absolute path; on a different machine, `File.Exists()` returns false gracefully - DLL scanning uses a hardcoded skip-list for known non-script assemblies (`System*`, `Microsoft*`, `GodotSharp`, etc.) - No C++ unit tests for `csharp_script.cpp` / `property_utils.cpp` changes (pre-existing test gap for this area) - PCK-based modding (loading assemblies from `.pck` at runtime) is not addressed — tracked separately in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/72159 and https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/109935 ## Scope and future work This PoC is intentionally focused on the core script discovery and registration problem. The `csharp://` path scheme is minimal — it enables `[GlobalClass]` and `[Export]` without changes to Godot's core resource system. The infrastructure (assembly scanning, `csharp://` loader) could be extended to support PCK-based modding in the future. I understand that a GDExtension migration ([godot-proposals#7895](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/7895)) may ultimately provide a more integrated solution. This PoC aims to solve the immediate need that users have had for 3+ years, in a way that's backward compatible and could coexist with or be replaced by a GDExtension approach. ## Related issues and PRs Addresses: - https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/75352 — Loading/assigning scripts from external assemblies fails - https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/77675 — Scripts cannot be loaded from additional C# projects - https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/95036 — GlobalClass from external assembly not in Create Node dialog - https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/104871 — External assembly inspector "out of date" warning - https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/100963 — Cannot organize code into multiple assemblies Related: - https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/1141 — Support multiple .NET SDK-style projects - https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/2646 — Allow project source files in subproject folder - https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/7895 — C# GDExtension Roadmap - https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/87753 — ScriptPathAttributeGenerator fails in test projects - https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/116812 — GlobalClass regression in 4.6.1 - https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/114868 — Prevent SourceGenerators transitive dependency - https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/72159 — PCK-based modding (separate scope) - https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/109935 — PCK assembly loading PR ## AI disclosure This contribution was developed with assistance from Claude (Anthropic). The AI was used for: codebase exploration, initial implementation drafting, and iterative refinement based on automated review feedback. All code was thoroughly reviewed, manually tested, and validated by the human contributor, who understands every part of the submission and can explain and maintain it independently.

items.title: Add support for `.opus` audio files

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

items.body:
This PR implements [godotengine/godot-proposals#6440](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/6440) by adding `AudioStreamOpus`, `AudioStreamPlaybackOpus` and `ResourceImporterOpus`. I have tested it on Windows and it works for all sample files at https://filesamples.com/formats/opus. ### Dependencies It adds the following thirdparty dependencies: - [xiph/opus](https://github.com/xiph/opus) - [xiph/opusfile](https://github.com/xiph/opusfile) The stream implementations of the PR are based on @mortarroad's PR in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/47114, although I had to modify them significantly. ### Screenshots
Click to expand
### Why? Without Opus, you have to use: - WAV - not compressed, unsuitable for long audio files. - Quite OK Audio is worse than Opus in every way except for CPU performance. - MP3 - released 34 years ago, very outdated compression, and [can't be looped seamlessly due to padding](https://sound.stackexchange.com/questions/25846/is-it-possible-to-loop-mp3-without-gaps). - Ogg Vorbis - released 26 years ago, outdated compression compared to Opus. In contrast, Opus is only 13 years old, with low latency and excellent compression. While most audio files on the internet are not using Opus, it's common for a file to be offered in WAV, which the Godot developer then has to convert to MP3/Vorbis to get a reasonable source control size. These files could be better compressed as Opus. The proposal in https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/6440 has 49 'likes' (compared to 1 'dislike') which shows others are interested in this. ### Footnotes Even though Opus files can be stored in `.ogg` containers, they need to be renamed to `.opus` to work with this PR. The impact on binary size of this PR is small: - Uncompressed: `182,486 KB` -> `182,719 KB` (increase: `233 KB`) - Compressed: `83,575 KB` -> `83,695 KB` (increase: `120 KB`) It may be possible to further reduce the binary size by removing unwanted files from xiph/opus and xiph/opusfile. I'm new to this so please let me know if I've done something wrong! :) - *Bugsquad edit:* This PR closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/6440

items.title: Add workflow support for OpenHarmony export templates

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

items.body:
<!--
Please target the `master` branch in priority.

Relevant fixes are cherry-picked for stable branches as needed by maintainers.

To speed up the contribution process and avoid CI errors, please set up pre-commit hooks locally:
https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/contributing/development/code_style_guidelines.html
-->

Follow-up to #108553.

Provides a workflow for building OpenHarmony export templates, making it easier for users to test without having to compile editors and export templates.

## Export the project

### Preparation

1. Download the editor and export templates from the [artifacts](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/109834/checks/) in Actions.[^1]
2. Download Commandline Tools, which currently requires API level 17+, that is, version 5.0.5+.[^2]
    - https://repo.huaweicloud.com/openharmony/ohpm/ (No registration required)
    - https://developer.huawei.com/consumer/en/download/command-line-tools-for-hmos (Registration required)
3. After extracting all the files, you will get a directory called `command-line-tools`, whose path is the path you need to fill in `export/openharmony/openharmony_tool_path` in the editor settings.
4. Download JDK, only JDK 17 is supported.[^3]
5. Please fill in the JDK path in `export/openharmony/java_sdk_path` in the editor settings.
6. Enable `textures/vram_compression/import_etc2_astc` in the project settings;

### Export the unsigned hap/app

Adds an OpenHarmony preset in the [export menu](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/tutorials/export/exporting_projects.html#export-menu). 

Check **Advanced Options**, and then specify `custom_template/debug` and `custom_template/release` as the export templates you just downloaded.[^4]

Make sure the export path does not contain special characters such as spaces.

### Prepare the material files required for signature[^5]

Signature material files can be generated by [DevEco Studio](https://developer.huawei.com/consumer/en/download/deveco-studio), but unfortunately DevEco Studio is not available on Linux.

You can also generate these files manually by following the steps below.

1. Create a keystore (.p12) file; [^6]
    ```shell
    keytool -genkeypair -alias "key_alias" -keyalg EC -sigalg "SHA256withECDSA" -keystore "store_file.p12" -storetype pkcs12 -storepass "StorePassword" -dname "CN=myapp.example.com, OU=IT Department, O=My Company, L=City, ST=State, C=Country" -keypass "StorePassword" -validity "3650"
    ```
2. Generate a certificate request (.csr) file;[^6][^7]
    ```shell

items.title: [Web] Add option to enable offscreen canvas

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

items.body:
This PR adds support for OffscreenCanvas. If we look at https://web.dev/articles/offscreen-canvas this seems to boost performance if used together with `proxy_to_pthread`. So it will try to use offscreen canvas if proxy to pthread is enabled, but disable it otherwise.

The link to proxy to pthread pr: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/79711. As of now Safari also supports it, and with `EMSCRIPTEN_WEBGL_CONTEXT_PROXY_FALLBACK` and enabled render via backbuffer it should also activate fallback if the offscreen canvas is not supported.

This is implemented as option, because it can also be enabled without proxy to pthread in both single and multi threaded builds. I'm not sure how useful it is, but it works.

This is mainly created so that the future C# multi-threading could be supported more easily. I don't know the full details of how it works, but the "main" C# thread is not a main runtime thread https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/101421, so because of it multi-threaded C# works similar to `proxy_to_pthread`.

It was tested locally with web editor build by creating a Mesh inside MeshInstance3D, and launching and stopping project several times, and a separate simple project that used a method that called `godot_webgl2_glGetBufferSubData` from the main thread and a new separate thread in both debug and release export.

The main downside is that after creating offscreen canvas from the canvas, you can't change width and height on the canvas directly, it needs to be changed on the resulted `OffscreenCanvas` object that we got from it. So I used `emscripten_set_canvas_element_size`/`emscripten_get_canvas_element_size`, it automatically forwards new sizes to the correct thread and changes canvas/offscreen canvas correctly, it also calls `resizeOffscreenFramebuffer` for us. And to make it possible to change sizes from outside of the module I also added a new method `setCanvasSize` to the `Engine`. 

Various other changes:
- Enabling proxy to pthread now disables xr automatically. For now webxr can't be used inside worker thread's main loop as it's not supported, see the link inside this comment https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/83733#issuecomment-4165775205 
- Removed `-sTEXTDECODER=0` as the support for the value 0 was removed entirely.
> TEXTDECODER[](https://emscripten.org/docs/tools_reference/settings_reference.html#textdecoder)
> The default value or 1 means the generated code will use TextDecoder if available and fall back to custom decoder code when not available. If set to 2, we assume TextDecoder is present and usable, and do not emit any JS code to fall back if it is missing. **Setting this zero to avoid even conditional usage of TextDecoder is no longer supported**. Note: In -Oz builds, the default value of TEXTDECODER is set to 2, to save on code size (except when AUDIO_WORKLET is specified, or when shell is part of ENVIRONMENT since TextDecoder is not available in those environments).
- Removed `_emscripten_proxy_main` from exported methods, it was undefined in both Emscripten 4.0.0 and the latest at the moment version, and builds fine without it.
- `file_access_unix.cpp` needed `<cstdlib>` in a single-threaded export build for `mkstemp`. `movie_writer_ogv.cpp` needed `<cstdlib>` for `rand` and `srand` in a single-threaded editor web build.
- Single-threaded web editor dev build complained about calling user callback after abort or `emscripten_force_exit`, so exit callback now cancels itself with `emscripten_cancel_main_loop`. It also crashed on `memdelete(os)`, but worked correctly after I changed it to normal `delete` to match the normal `new` it was created with. Multi-threaded web editor worked fine, so I'm not sure why single-threaded build behaved this way.

items.title: Add AsyncPCK support (+ Web implementation)
items.body:
**Note:** This PR has been superseded by #116673.
Table of Contents - [What are AsyncPCKs?](#user-content-asyncpck-what-are-asyncpcks) - [Why AsyncPCKs are needed in Godot?](#user-content-asyncpck-why-asyncpcks-are-needed) - [How does it work?](#user-content-how-does-it-work) - [We are installing files, now?](#user-content-we-are-installing-files-now) - [`AsyncPCKInstaller` node to the rescue!](#user-content-asyncpckinstaller-node-to-the-rescue) - [See it for yourself (demo)](#user-content-see-it-for-yourself-demo) - ["Resource remaps", a must-have addon for porting to the Web](#user-content-a-must-have-addon-for-porting-to-the-web) - [Conclusion](#user-content-conclusion)
Introducing AsyncPCKs.

What are AsyncPCKs?

This PR adds AsyncPCK as a new [resource pack](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/export/exporting_pcks.html#overview-of-pck-zip-files) "format" for Godot. AsyncPCK are essentially an "unpacked" version of standard `.pck` file in a `.asyncpck` directory instead.

Why AsyncPCKs are needed?

Currently, the Web platform export games essentially the same way desktop games do. On export, it creates these files: - the required Web files for the browser (HTML and style files). - Godot JavaScript files to interface between the engine and the browser. - a [WebAssembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WebAssembly) `.wasm` file containing the engine executable. - Equivalent to `my_project.exe` when exporting to Windows. - the assets of the project in a `.pck` file. - Equivalent to `my_project.pck` when exporting on desktop platforms. On Desktop and Mobile platforms, disk accesses are essentially taken as granted. So, when asking for `res://my_image.png`, the Godot engine opens the `.pck` file and finds the image file at a given offset on the disk. On the Web platform, resources are remote. This complicates things, as the engine (and most game engines) expect resources to be available near instantly. To fix this issue, the Godot JavaScript files make sure to download and install (in the virtual filesystem for the WASM file) the project `.pck` file before launching the game. So everything's fine, right? The problem for the Web platform lies with the size of that `.pck` file. It can get big quite quickly (by Web standards). By default, the exported `.pck` contains every resource of the project. This means that the game will only start the game once every asset is loaded, including the final boss' ones. **This is bad.** This is not ideal because players are usually impatient, especially on specialized websites like [Poki](https://poki.com/) or [CrazyGames](https://www.crazygames.com/). On these websites, players land on your game to play something, not necessarily to play your game in particular (vs opening a gamejam entry on [itch.io](https://itch.io/)).

How does it work?

As AsyncPCK are essentially just "unpacked" PCKs, it works 98% the same, but the files are exposed in a directory on export. The export process must add metadata for each exported asset. These `.deps.json` files contain the list of every dependencies (recursively). The dependencies are checked only _after_ export, as it's not possible to do so before on the export dialog (limitation of Godot due to the possibility of export plugins to modify or remap resources).
menu.gd.deps.json generated from Catburglar ```json { "dependencies": { "res://scripts/menu.gd": [ "res://scripts/settings.gd", "res://sprites/ui/menu/cursor.png" ], "res://scripts/settings.gd": [], "res://sprites/ui/menu/cursor.png": [] }, "resources": { "res://scripts/menu.gd": { "files": { "res://scripts/menu.gd.remap": { "size": 39 }, "res://scripts/menu.gdc": { "size": 2613 } }, "totalSize": 2652 }, "res://scripts/settings.gd": { "files": { "res://scripts/settings.gd.remap": { "size": 43 }, "res://scripts/settings.gdc": { "size": 5634 } }, "totalSize": 5677 }, "res://sprites/ui/menu/cursor.png": { "files": { "res://.godot/imported/cursor.png-9b2f19c8ebb7ebafbffb55bc49257263.ctex": { "size": 150 }, "res://sprites/ui/menu/cursor.png.import": { "size": 195 } }, "totalSize": 345 } } } ```
This file is quite handy on the Web for the Godot JavaScript middlelayer. This makes it possible for it to download and install in the virutal filesystem every dependency listed. Here's a diagram of the `AsyncPCK` install process as implemented for the Web platform. ```mermaid --- title: "[Web] AsyncPCK install and loading process" --- sequenceDiagram participant Game participant OS as OS
(singleton) participant Browser as Browser
(Godot middlelayer) participant Server Game ->>+ OS: `OS.async_pck_is_supported()` note over Game, OS: [Web] Returns `true`.
[Other] Returns `false`. OS ->>- Game: `true` Game ->>+ OS: `OS.async_pck_is_file_installable("res://level1.tscn")` note over Game, OS: [AsyncPCK export] Returns `true`.
[Standard PCK export] Returns `false`. OS ->>- Game: `true` %% [Install file] Game ->>+ OS: `OS.async_pck_install_file("res://level1.tscn")` OS ->> OS: Get the related PCK of "res://level1.tscn". OS ->>+ Browser: Install "res://level1.tscn" from "index.asyncpck" Browser ->>+ Server: Fetch "index.asyncpck/assets/level1.tscn.deps.json" Server ->>- Browser: ["level1.tscn.deps.json" contents] note over Browser, Server: Lists "level1.tscn" (50KiB) and "level1.webp" (500KiB). Browser ->>+ Server: Fetch files listed in "level1.tscn.deps.json" Browser ->>- OS: `Error.OK` OS ->>- Game: `Error.OK` %% [Install file] END %% [Fetch progress] loop Fetch progress Server ->> Browser: Update fetch progress of files listed in "level1.tscn.deps.json". end %% [Fetch progress] END %% [Get status file] loop Update install status Game ->>+ OS: `OS.async_pck_install_file_get_status("res://level1.tscn")` OS ->> OS: Get the related PCK of "res://level1.tscn". OS ->>+ Browser: Get install status of "res://level1.tscn" from "index.asyncpck" Browser ->>- OS: Install status of "res://level1.tscn" OS ->>- Game: Install status of "res://level1.tscn" end note right of Game: The game can display
a progress bar. %% [Get status file] END Server ->>- Browser: Fetch done. Browser ->> Browser: Install files in WASM virtual file system. note over Game, Browser: The game will realize that files are installed
in the [Update install status] loop. Game ->> Game: `load("res://level1.tscn")` ```

We are installing files, now?

"Install" is the most appropriate word I could find to describe this process, as "load" is already a term users actually use in their projects to load assets in their game. In the context of AsyncPCKs, "installing" means to make the file available to "load". For the Web platform, it implies downloading the file first.

AsyncPCKInstaller node to the rescue!

In order to simplify this heavy install process for users, this PR also introduces the new `AsyncPCKInstaller` node. It's a very simple node that does the heavy polling and checks in the background and triggers signals for users instead. | Inspector view | Signals view | | :---: | :---: | | ![asyncpckinstaller_inspector](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/43fb52af-6553-4c6f-acdc-f4ecbc028d80) | ![asyncpckinstaller_signals](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/27b37bd5-cec6-4172-85e4-f75185aa1476) | It's made to be compatible with non-AsyncPCK exports too! Ideally, you can create your game all around supporting AsyncPCKs even if they are not needed for specific exports. The node will just emit the signals signalling that the files are ready pretty much instantly.

See it for yourself (demo)

|| Link | Initial load size | | :---: | :---: | :---: | | Sync Catburglar | [Link](https://godot-asyncpck-catburglar-sync.adamscott.studio/) | ~32MiB | | Async Catburglar | [Link](https://godot-asyncpck-catburglar-async.adamscott.studio/) | ~10MiB |
> [!NOTE] > If you're interested in porting an existing game to the Web using this PR, please read the following about the "Resource Remaps" addon and about my plea to merge the feature into core.

"Resource Remaps", a must-have addon for porting to the Web

 I'm talking about the [Resource Remaps](https://godotengine.org/asset-library/asset/3451) addon by @allenwp. One of the first things I realized when I started using my PR to port [Catburglar](https://bitbucket.org/JohnGabrielUK/catburglar/src) ([itch.io link](https://johngabrieluk.itch.io/catburglar)) was the need to be able to remap assets to one and another for the Web. In Catburglar, it uses a required intro video that is at least 1.5MiB in size. It's quite a chunky download that adds quite a lot to the initial download size. I created a compressed version (it shows a little bit), but I didn't necessarily want to replace the original video. Following the "Godot way" of doing things, only one game project should be needed for every exports. So I had two choices. The first was to get deep into the code in order to add dynamic checks to check the current platform and replace each place that requires the video (animation players, scenes, scripts and more) depending on the result. This is huge and really not efficient. The other is just to remap the video to another one on export. This is exactly what the Resource Remaps addon does. Honestly, as the Web platform is so different of others in terms of soft requirements, I really think that one cannot port an existing game to the Web without interchanging assets. Or even whole scenes. **That's why I hereby plead to merge this addon in the Engine natively.** (i.e. to reopen godotengine/godot-proposals#10051)

Conclusion

This PR will revolutionize IMHO Godot's pertinence as a tool to create games to the Web platform. By making the initial download as small as possible, users will be able to use their favorite game engine to create legitimate and competitive games on the platform.

items.title: iOS 4.6.2 export template ships broken arm64 simulator xcframework slice on Apple Silicon
items.body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in 4.6.2.stable
Works in 4.6.1

### System information

Godot v4.6.2.stable - macOS Tahoe (26.4.0) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M1 Pro (Apple7) - Apple M1 Pro (10 threads) - 16.00 GiB memory

### Issue description

The shipped iOS export template appears to advertise arm64 simulator support, but the actual simulator libgodot archive only contains x86_64.

On Apple Silicon Macs, this causes iOS simulator builds from the exported Xcode project to fail with many undefined Godot symbols, because Xcode selects the arm64 simulator target but the bundled libgodot.a does not actually contain an arm64 simulator slice.

What I expected:
  The iOS simulator xcframework slice `ios-arm64_x86_64-simulator` should contain both `arm64` and `x86_64`, matching the
  xcframework metadata.

  What happens instead:
  The archive at:

  ~/Library/Application Support/Godot/export_templates/4.6.2.stable/ios.zip
    -> libgodot.ios.debug.xcframework/ios-arm64_x86_64-simulator/libgodot.a

  is x86_64-only.

  This causes exported iOS projects to fail to link for Apple Silicon simulators.

  Typical linker errors:
  - Undefined symbol: _err_print_error(...)
  - Undefined symbol: _err_flush_stdout()
  - Undefined symbol: Dictionary::Dictionary()
  - many other Godot C++ symbols

The simulator xcframework metadata claims arm64 support, but the actual archive does not contain it.

  For example, after extracting the iOS template zip:

  ```bash
  lipo -info libgodot.ios.debug.xcframework/ios-arm64_x86_64-simulator/libgodot.a

  reports only:

  x86_64

  However, the xcframework slice is named:

  ios-arm64_x86_64-simulator


### Steps to reproduce

  1. Install Godot 4.6.2.stable export templates.
  2. Export an iOS project.
  3. Open the generated Xcode project on an Apple Silicon Mac.
  4. Build for a normal iPhone/iPad simulator.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A Happens with all projects.

items.title: OpenXR: Add support for Foveated Inset

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

items.body: This PR implements support for OpenXR Foveated inset rendering if supported by the hardware. When using foveated inset rendering, the main viewport output renders a high FOV, lower resolution render which is augmented with a separate high resolution render pass at the users focal point. A good overview of the technique is explained [on Varjos website here](https://varjo.com/blog/make-the-best-out-of-your-varjo-experience-update-on-varjo-quad-view-eye-tracked-foveation-and-varjo-base-settings). In order for the user to have quality control and ensure the camera settings can be configured, this PR introduces a new viewport node that controls the rendering of the foveated inset: An extra `XROrigin3D` node is required with a few lines of code so it is placed in the same location as the main `XROrigin3D` node. We also have a separate `XRCamera3D` node with it's `tracker' set to 'inset` (note that I am still working on a nice solution for the dropdown here). Todos: - [ ] Loads of testing (few runtimes support this at the moment so this will be tricky). - [ ] Make sure we have proper feedback if inset rendering is enabled but our viewport is not supplied or incorrectly configured. - [ ] Figure out whether we need to worry about this being used in conjunction with frame synthesis and/or VRS. - [ ] Improve tracker selection dropdown (might become a separate PR). This logic is all based on https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/115799 (merged) and https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/116424 A sample project can be found [here](https://codeberg.org/BastiaanOlij/test-foveated-inset). This PR supersedes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/81505 and https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/108156

items.title: [Web] Bus.addAt(-1) scrambles JS bus array, silently disconnecting Master from destination on Sample playback
items.body:
### Tested versions
- Reproduces on v4.6.2.stable Web export, single-threaded (`variant/thread_support=false`).
- Reproduces in 4.3+ since [#91382](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/91382) introduced sample playback for web; the bug is in code that hasn't materially changed since.

### System information
Firefox 121, Chrome 121 (desktop + mobile), itch.io hosting (no COOP/COEP). Same symptom when serving the build over local `python -m http.server`.

### Issue description
Every `AudioStreamPlayer` using `PLAYBACK_TYPE_SAMPLE` (which is the per-platform default for web since 4.3 via `audio/general/default_playback_type.web=Sample`) is silent on the deployed HTML5 build if the project has more than one audio bus. `AudioStreamPlayer.playing` stays `true`, all bus volumes look healthy, but bus peak meters sit at `-inf`. Local desktop is unaffected.

The C++ side correctly produces sample data — confirmed by reading the `AudioBuffer` channel data in DevTools after `register_stream`: `maxAmplitude L=R=1.008` for a normalized .wav. The `SampleNode` lifecycle runs cleanly to `_source.start()` (`isStarted=true`, `AudioBufferSourceNode.buffer` is set). Yet no audio reaches `ctx.destination` because Master's `_send` ends up reassigned away from `null`, and `Bus.connect()` severs Master's connection to `ctx.destination`.

### Root cause
`Bus.addAt(-1)` in `platform/web/js/libs/library_godot_audio.js`:

```js
static addAt(index) {
    const newBus = GodotAudio.Bus.create();      // appends to end
    if (index !== newBus.getId()) {              // -1 !== newId, fires
        GodotAudio.Bus.move(newBus.getId(), index);  // move(N, -1) - buggy
    }
}
```

`AudioServer::add_bus(p_at_pos)` (`servers/audio/audio_server.cpp`) normalizes `p_at_pos >= buses.size()` to `-1` ("append") and forwards via `add_sample_bus(p_at_pos)`. JS `Bus.create()` correctly pushes to the end, but the `if` then fires and calls `Bus.move(N, -1)`. `Bus.move`'s body does `splice(toIndex - 1, 0, item)` = `splice(-2, 0, item)`, inserting at `length - 2` instead of at end, scrambling the JS bus array relative to C++. Subsequent `set_bus_send` calls land on the wrong buses; eventually Master's `_send` is reassigned to a non-null bus, and `Bus.connect()` calls `getOutputNode().disconnect()` on Master, cutting it off from `ctx.destination`.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Empty Godot 4.6.2 project, web export, `variant/thread_support=false`.
2. Add 2+ audio buses (e.g. via a `default_bus_layout.tres` containing Master + Music + SFX, or via `AudioServer.add_bus()` in an autoload's `_ready()`).
3. Play any `AudioStreamPlayer` with `playback_type=PLAYBACK_TYPE_SAMPLE` on the deployed build.
4. Audio is silent. Master bus peak is `-inf`.

### Diagnostic logs (post-export instrumentation)
Pre-fix (broken):

```
register_stream framesTotal=3700 sampleRate=48000 maxAmplitude L=1.008 R=1.008
before setVolume: options.volume=[1,1,0,0,0,0,0,0]
busId=0 bus._gainNode.gain=1 bus._soloNode.gain=1 bus._muteNode.gain=1 bus._send=3   <- BUG
after setVolume gains: L=1 R=1 C=0 LFE=0 SL=0 SR=0
this.start() returned isStarted=true
```

Post-fix (audible) on the same build with the patch applied:

```
busId=0 ... bus._send=null(direct to destination)   <- FIXED
```

### Fix
PR submitted: will be linked once filed (this issue first to get the number).

Single-line guard in `Bus.addAt`: skip `Bus.move` when `index === -1`.

---

*Investigation and writeup drafted with assistance from Claude Sonnet 4.6; root cause confirmed and fix verified by @bziebart123 on a deployed itch.io build before submitting.*
